timeline_reviews.summary: Transport stream source; manifest records no projected semantic events, but it accounts for the raw CLI stream.
Serial parent timeline: single-agent probing, implementation writes, syntax fix, smoke checks, and long unfinished differential run.

parallel.requirements: Port the networkx script to zero-dependency Node.js ESM under /output, matching CLI parsing, exact printed values, formatting, and executable behavior.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent owned implementation and local integration while delegating black-box probing and later adversarial verification to workflow children.
parallel.implementation: The parent created Python-style repr/int helpers, graph data structures, traversal, shortest path, MST, connectivity, CLI parsing, index barrel, and /output/test10.mjs.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The implementation was assembled in /output; artifact validation copied test10.mjs and local modules, including the late formatter file.
parallel.verification: The parent ran sample probes, CLI/error checks, unit checks, a 371-case differential sweep, and launched a verifier workflow that did not return a final report.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The agent process timed out; both workflows were killed with null aggregate results, and the final formatter change was not covered by a later parent-side full differential run.

serial.requirements: Same prompt and requirements: pure JS ESM modules in /output, no external dependencies, manual CLI behavior, and exact networkx output matching.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One parent actor handled probing, coding, integration, and checking because workflow and delegation tools were disabled in the serial control.
serial.implementation: The serial parent created formatting, CLI, graph, structure, and algorithm modules, wrote /output/test10.mjs, and repaired a syntax error in pyint.mjs.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial artifact included the entrypoint and module tree; artifact validation copied the expected files from /output successfully.
serial.verification: The serial run performed manual behavior probes, a post-fix smoke test, and started a broad local differential harness that was killed before completion.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The process timed out with the long local differential test returning exit 137, but the current official evaluator completed and passed 160/160.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Recognized the same Py2JS task: pure Node.js ESM modules, manual CLI parsing, no external dependencies, byte-matching networkx outputs, and /output/test10.mjs delivery.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Recognized the same prompt requirements and executable-only black-box observation rule in the serial control.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirements difference; both ultimately produced artifacts passing the current 160-sample official evaluation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent split probing and verification into workflow children while keeping implementation ownership in the parent-written /output tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had workflow and delegation tools disabled and performed probing, coding, and checks in one parent timeline.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used broad child fan-out for investigation/verification; serial used a direct single-agent path without subagent ownership boundaries.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Child briefs carried detailed executable and matching requirements, but they also directed children to use shared /workspace/tmp scratch paths.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial control kept all task knowledge in one timeline and did not transfer work through child briefs or reports.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No retained missing-context label; the main difference is that parallel context transfer introduced shared scratch conventions absent in serial.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent wrote a modular port under /output/lib/python, /output/lib/graph, /output/lib/cli, and /output/test10.mjs before later adding formatter support.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial parent wrote its own modular port with format, CLI, graph, structures, and algorithm modules, then fixed an initial pyint syntax problem.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implemented full graph and CLI behavior but used different module layouts and different local correction paths.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Probe and verifier workflows were launched, but their aggregate results remained null when killed; some child findings existed below the workflow layer.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were no child results to retrieve; the only long-running local differential process ended with an exit-137 notification near timeout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had child-result lifecycle loss from killed workflows, whereas serial had an unfinished local background test rather than an unreturned child aggregate.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children used shared /workspace/tmp and two children observed another agent overwriting their scratch harnesses or outputs before isolating.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no workflow children or shared child scratch state; its scratch and implementation actions were from one actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had concrete artifact leakage in shared temporary files; serial did not have an analogous shared-state boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran hand-picked checks and a 371-case differential sweep, then made a later formatter change and launched an adversarial verifier workflow that was killed before report.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran local smoke tests after fixing syntax and started a broad differential test that was killed, but the official evaluator later passed 160/160.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both had incomplete pre-timeout verification, but parallel additionally invalidated its completed sweep with a later implementation change and lost the verifier workflow report.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed 24 subagent logs, over 2.8M total tokens, and timed out with process returncode 143 despite an artifact that later passed official evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out but with no subagents and fewer total tokens; it left a slow local differential run unfinished while still passing official evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both exceeded the agent process budget, but parallel uniquely spent substantial budget on workflow fan-out and stalled children.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome: both completed official evaluations passed 160 of 160 samples. The concrete difference is process-level: parallel used broad workflows that caused shared scratch contamination, killed aggregate workflow results, and a late post-sweep formatter write; serial used a single-agent path with no delegation and no shared child scratch, but also timed out after starting a slow local differential run.
parallel_contributors: Workflow fan-out produced many stalled or killed child attempts and consumed budget before the verifier could return an aggregate report.
Shared /workspace/tmp scratch use caused child harness contamination and rework.
A formatter file was added after the completed 371-case sweep without a later parent-side full rerun before timeout.
serial_contributors: Serial kept implementation and verification in one actor, avoiding child handoff and shared child-scratch boundaries.
Serial fixed its syntax error before later smoke and differential attempts, then passed the same official evaluation.
ordinary_implementation_differences: The two passing artifacts used different module organization and helper names.
Serial long differential testing was too slow and ended with exit 137, but this was a local verification budget issue rather than a parallel coordination pattern.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained labels describe realized parallel-side adverse process episodes only

Rejected: the parent wrote the required /output/test10.mjs entrypoint and the artifact validator copied the expected deliverable.
Rejected: the parent actively managed probing, implementation, local checks, and delivery; the later issue was budget and verification timing, not absent pipeline ownership.
Rejected: implementation was not blocked behind one mandatory serial preflight; the parent wrote modules while probes were still running.

Rejected: the direct allocation problem was broad workflow fan-out and retries exhausting the budget, not capacity shifted from one identifiable critical path.

The parallel parent launched two broad workflows with many child agents and repeated stall retries. The workflow state records show both workflows killed with aggregate results still null, while the cell hit the agent timeout. The serial control had workflows disabled and no subagents, so this was a parallel-only budget and result-lifecycle cost even though the submitted artifact later passed official evaluation.
candidates.realized_consequence: Both parallel workflows were killed with null aggregate results after broad child fan-out and retries, leaving the parent without the intended synthesized probe spec or final verifier report before the run timed out.
candidates.near_match_reason: The absent verifier report was downstream of broad workflow fan-out and retries exhausting the run budget, not a single concrete verifier finding trapped below the parent.

candidates.reason: Rejected: killed or interrupted children are part of the same workflow fan-out timeout chain and no separate needed child result was deliberately stopped before finalization.
Rejected: a complete deliverable was already present in /output; the issue is not a ready candidate left unpromoted.

The parent completed a 371-case integrated differential sweep, then found help wrapping still diverged and wrote a new formatter file afterward. No later parent-side integrated rerun closed that verification loop before the timeout, while the serial run fixed its syntax issue before its later checks rather than changing the implementation after a completed sweep.
candidates.realized_consequence: The completed 371-case sweep no longer covered the final artifact after the late formatter change, so the final tree entered timeout without a parent-side post-change integrated check.
candidates.near_match_reason: There was no explicit whole-task completion acceptance by the parent; the directly visible problem is the ordering of a late implementation change after earlier verification.

candidates.reason: Rejected: implementation was written by the parent, not completed by a child and then left unjoined.
Rejected: the missing verifier aggregate is downstream of the broad fan-out budget exhaustion episode, not an independent trapped concrete finding.
Rejected: stalled and killed probe or verifier children did not own required implementation work needing takeover; the retained fan-out label covers the result loss.
Rejected: there is no concrete completed child result received by the parent and then ignored inconsistently; returned probe material was either used or never aggregated.
Rejected: the parent continued local inspection and verification activity; timeout symptoms are better explained by workflow fan-out exhaustion.
Rejected: concurrent children did not write competing implementation files with overlapping behavior in the final source tree.
Rejected: the observed overwrites were temporary harness artifacts, not two live agents editing the same source/configuration file.
Rejected: no non-entry library or module source produced by another actor was replaced or recreated by a concurrent actor.
Rejected: the required entrypoint or submitted artifact was not overwritten by another live owner.
Rejected: no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced another actor’s final-tree work.
Rejected: shared-write evidence is more specifically artifact leakage in temporary harness scripts, and no broader final-workspace provenance problem is proven.

The workflow instructed concurrent children to use the shared /workspace/tmp scratch area. Two probe children later observed helper scripts or outputs being overwritten by another agent and had to move into private subdirectories before their tests were trustworthy. The serial control had no child agents and no shared workflow scratch contention.
candidates.realized_consequence: Child probe harnesses consumed overwritten shared temporary artifacts, producing corrupted or misleading intermediate runs and forcing rework in isolated scratch directories.
candidates.near_match_reason: The observed collision was consumption of contaminated temporary scripts and outputs, not merely multiple agents writing a shared implementation workspace without a more specific artifact leak.

cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; retained labels cover the only directly evidenced independent parallel coordination boundaries with realized consequences.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: Rejected labels are not added for ordinary coding work, official timeout alone, child count alone, unavailable workflow reports already covered by fan-out, or speculative context defects.
